finding: The original B16 queue specification reserved 4 GiB RSS plus the queue 1 GiB safety headroom. Host available memory was about 4.17 GiB, so the queued units were not admitted before child creation. Completed B10 fits with the same data/architecture except six extra bits measured 495845376 and 480378880 bytes maximum RSS.
old_real_outputs: NONE; old B16 units remained queued, no scientific child or role read.
operational_change: Use a 2 GiB RSS reservation for new B16 replacement unit IDs; this exceeds measured B10 peak by more than fourfold. Keep CPU/wall budgets, bits, model/loss/selection, source pins, role permissions and point gates unchanged.
supersession: Preserve old queued specs and report them as superseded. New specs must pin this committed amendment and otherwise match old specs except unit ID, output paths and max_rss_gib.
